identity.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

baseTree.use: older-fork: the heir is made by a child process of this recorder on this tree (Node as shipped, without the fix)

clock: Date.now() stands still at 1800000000000 for the whole run (lib/mc-record.mjs freezeClock); every sidecar's mtime is 1799996400000 (an hour older): the prune's ten-minute age gate reads both
command: node benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/record-offload-prune-order.mjs --tree <export of b6f10295a2f698afc85332467192de28500bd146 with the patch> --patch benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/patches/node-fix-prune-after-save.patch --base-tree <export of b6f10295a2f698afc85332467192de28500bd146>

exclusions.clearedEnvironment: after a clear the core's header holds the environment block written for the next request (sessionStartMetaInjected false); Node keeps it outside `messages` (resetSessionBp3Environment, session-crud.mjs) until that request, so the transcript compared after a clear leaves that block out
exclusions.forks: clear-fork, heir-fork, older-fork, unreadable-fork, linkless-fork, deleted-middle and copy-in-progress record the cleared session's directory and transcript; the fork's and the heirs' transcripts are not compared (the carry into them is recorded elsewhere): what they keep is the sidecar they name, which the cleared session's directory shows
exclusions.linklessFork: linkless-fork's seed holds the shipped fork's id and stored transcript as the replay's input (the core's migration derives the fork's reference set from it); the fork itself is not compared
exclusions.olderForkHeir: older-fork's seed holds the heir's source link and the conversation it carries (its non-system messages) as the replay's input; the heir's system prompt (composed for its own minted id) is left out, and its minted id is <HEIR>
exclusions.referenceSets: Node's stored reference sets (offload-sources.json in the data dir, and each record's offloadSources) are Node's format and not compared; the core holds the same sets in each session's header and its index: what they keep shows in the directories recorded
exclusions.roomLog: room-row's seed holds the room log's stored messages as the replay's input; the room log itself is not compared
exclusions.sessionFiles: the session store's own files (sessions/<id>.json, <id>.log.jsonl) are Node's format; the core's store writes its own record log, so their names and bytes are not compared: the stored transcript is, whole, as each store reads it back
exclusions.summary: the summary is a scripted provider answer naming the kept sidecar; the compaction itself is recorded elsewhere (compaction-commit)
exclusions.systemMessageMeta: the core holds a session's system prompt in its header's prompt blocks (as the migration stores Node's leading system messages), which carry no message meta: the `meta` (transcript messageId) Node's compaction stamps on its system message is not compared; its role, content and cache tier are

normalised.attemptId: a turn completion's `attemptId` (meta.transcript.completion, cancelled-turn and failed-turn) is a random UUID on both sides: it is <ATTEMPT>
normalised.completionVerb: a turn completion's `verb` is the client's label: Node's runtime has none without a client (`failedTurnCompletion`'s `Thought`), the core's `turn/start` stamps the client's `pickDoneVerb(stats.turns)` (`Mapped` for its first turn); it is <VERB>
normalised.dataDir: the data dir is a temporary one: every string naming it names <DATA>
normalised.summaryHash: the summary header's `sha256=` hashes the dropped messages, which name the temporary data dir: it is <SHA>
